message: The $10,000 website is the model, not the skill
yt_title: The $10,000 website isn't the skill. It's the model.
yt_desc:
Everyone is saying a free design skill plus Claude Opus builds you a website an agency would charge $10,000 for.

That line sounds like it's about the skill. It isn't. Open one — they're just text files. A skill is a markdown file with a settings block at the top, sitting in a folder the agent reads. No code runs.

The good ones do three things: interview you before they build, route work between models, and argue with themselves before they start. All three are process, not taste. You could do them by hand. The value is that you don't have to remember to.

Full breakdown on the channel.

lines.text: Everyone is saying the same thing. A free design skill plus Claude builds you a website an agency would charge ten thousand for.
That line sounds like it is about the skill. It is not. It is about the model.
Because if you actually open one of these skills, they are just text files. You can read them.
A skill is a markdown file with a settings block at the top, sitting in a folder the agent reads. No code runs.
The good ones do three things. They interview you before building, they route work between models, and they argue with themselves before they start.
All three are process, not taste. You could do them by hand. The value is that you do not have to remember to.
